Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it

The main database is the only store: do not introduce another database, a cache or a search engine unasked; first show the access pattern that the main database cannot serve.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: I prefer typed columns and tables to JSON columns.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Reads go to: Read replicas, when a little lag is acceptable
Send only reads that tolerate lag to the read replica connection; read from the primary inside a transaction and right after a write, so that a user always sees what they just changed.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Large tables are: Neither partitioned nor sharded
Tables are neither partitioned nor sharded: do not introduce either unasked; propose it with the table size and the query that needs it.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Large tables are: Partitioned (by date, by tenant…)

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Large tables are: Sharded across several databases
Data is sharded: every query carries the shard key, no join or transaction crosses shards, a row’s shard key never changes, and a new table states its shard key before any code is written.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Every query goes through one shared connection pool.
Take database connections from the shared pool only and release them on every path (`finally`, or the ORM’s own handling); never open a connection per request, hold one across a slow call, or raise the pool size to hide a slow query.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Every query goes through one shared connection pool.
Connection handling is left to the platform (serverless driver, external pooler): do not add a pool or change connection settings unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: List endpoints are paginated with: A page number and a page size
Paginate every list endpoint with a page number and a page size, with a default and a maximum page size, a stable sort order, and the same response envelope as the existing lists.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: List endpoints are paginated with: A cursor (keyset)
Paginate every list endpoint with an opaque cursor over a unique, indexed sort key (keyset), with a maximum page size; never use `OFFSET` on a table that grows.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: List endpoints are paginated with: Nothing: lists are returned whole
Lists are returned whole: do not add pagination unasked, but say when a new list has no upper bound.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The API version is carried by: The URL (`/v1/…`)
Put every new route under the current version prefix (`/v1/...`); a breaking change goes under a new prefix, and the old one keeps working until its removal is announced.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The API version is carried by: A header or a media type
The API version comes from a request header: read it through the existing helper, treat a missing one as the existing routes do, and never put a version in a URL.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The API version is carried by: Nothing: there is one version
The API has one version: do not add a version prefix or header unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The API is described by: An OpenAPI (or schema) file written before the code
The API description is written first: change the OpenAPI or schema file before the code, then make the code match it, with every status code and error shape the endpoint can return.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The API is described by: A description generated from the code
The API description is generated from the code: keep the route schemas and types it reads complete, regenerate it with the project’s command after any change to a route, and never edit the generated file by hand.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The API is described by: No formal description
There is no formal API description: do not add one unasked; document a new or changed endpoint where the existing ones are documented.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Callers are authenticated with: A server-side session behind a cookie
Sessions live on the server behind a cookie set `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax` or stricter: never put a session id or a token in `localStorage` or a URL, renew the session id at login, and protect state-changing routes against CSRF.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Callers are authenticated with: JWT access tokens
Access tokens are JWTs: verify signature, expected algorithm, issuer, audience and expiry on every request with the project’s helper, keep their lifetime short (5 to 15 minutes) next to a revocable refresh token, and never put a secret in the payload.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Callers are authenticated with: Opaque tokens or API keys
Callers send an opaque token in `Authorization: Bearer`: store only its hash, show the value once at creation, give each token scopes and an expiry, and never accept one from a query string.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Callers are authenticated with: An external identity provider (OpenID Connect, SAML)
Sign-in is delegated to an identity provider: use the authorization code flow with PKCE, validate `state` and the ID token (signature, issuer, audience, expiry), take the identity from the ID token, and never add a password login next to it.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Callers are authenticated with: Something else
Callers are authenticated with {value}: reuse the existing mechanism, and never add a second one next to it.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Every route checks, on the server, that the caller may act on that exact resource.
On every route that reads or changes a resource, check through the project’s authorization helper that it belongs to the caller; never trust an id from the URL or the body, and add a test that tries another user’s resource.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Every route checks, on the server, that the caller may act on that exact resource.
Access is checked by a layer above the handlers (gateway, global guard): do not repeat the check in each handler, but say when a new route is not covered by it.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Passwords are hashed with: Argon2id
Hash passwords with Argon2id through the project’s helper, with a salt per password and a cost tuned to about 100 to 300 ms; never use MD5, SHA-1 or SHA-256 for a password, even salted.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Passwords are hashed with: bcrypt
Hash passwords with bcrypt through the project’s helper; bcrypt ignores what comes after 72 bytes, so cap the accepted length, and never use MD5, SHA-1 or SHA-256 for a password, even salted.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Passwords are hashed with: scrypt
Hash passwords with scrypt through the project’s helper, with a salt per password; never use MD5, SHA-1 or SHA-256 for a password, even salted.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Passwords are hashed with: Nothing: the application stores no password
The application stores no password: never add a password column, a password login or a reset flow; sign-in stays with the existing provider.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Cross-origin requests from browsers (CORS) are: Allowed for a list of known origins
CORS allows the origins of the configured list only: add an origin to that list, never answer `*` or reflect the `Origin` header, and never combine a wildcard with credentials.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Cross-origin requests from browsers (CORS) are: Not allowed: the front end is on the same origin
The API sends no CORS headers because the front end is on the same origin: do not enable CORS to make a call pass.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Cross-origin requests from browsers (CORS) are: Allowed for any origin, without credentials (public API)
CORS is open to any origin because the API is public: keep it without credentials (no cookies), and authenticate with a token in a header.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Security headers (HSTS, Content-Security-Policy, `X-Content-Type-Options`…) are set by: The application (helmet or the framework’s equivalent)
Security headers are set in one place in the application (HSTS, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, frame and content security policies): change them there, never per route, and never loosen a policy (`unsafe-inline`, `*`) without asking.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Security headers (HSTS, Content-Security-Policy, `X-Content-Type-Options`…) are set by: The reverse proxy or the CDN
Security headers are set by the reverse proxy or the CDN: do not set them again in application code; when a change needs a header or a looser policy, say which one and where.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Security headers (HSTS, Content-Security-Policy, `X-Content-Type-Options`…) are set by: Nobody yet
No security headers are set yet: do not add a library for them unasked, but say so when a change serves HTML or sets a cookie.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The back end also: Renders HTML or emails that contain user content
Escape user content by default wherever it reaches HTML or an email, through the template engine’s auto-escaping; never build markup by string concatenation, and never mark user content as safe.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The back end also: Fetches URLs given by users (webhooks, imports, previews)
Before fetching a URL given by a user, allow only `http` and `https`, resolve the host and refuse private, loopback, link-local and cloud metadata addresses, do not follow redirects unchecked, and set a timeout and a size limit.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The back end also: Accepts file uploads
For an upload, check type and size at the boundary, never trust the client’s file name or content type, store it outside the web root under a generated name, and serve it back with an explicit `Content-Type`.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The back end also: Runs commands or opens paths built from input
Never pass input to a shell: use `execFile` or `spawn` with an argument array and no `shell` option, and resolve any path built from input against a fixed base folder, refusing what escapes it.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The back end also: None of these
The back end renders no HTML, fetches no user-given URL, takes no upload and runs no command: when a change would start doing one of these, say so first.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: GET responses state how they may be cached (`Cache-Control`, `ETag`).
Set `Cache-Control` on every GET response: `public, max-age` only when the answer is the same for every caller, `private` or `no-store` for anything tied to a user or a token, and an `ETag` answered with 304 where clients revalidate.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: GET responses state how they may be cached (`Cache-Control`, `ETag`).
Do not add caching headers or ETags unasked: responses are not meant to be cached by clients or by a CDN.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: On the server, computed or fetched data is cached in: A shared cache (Redis, Memcached…)
Cache through the project’s cache helper on the shared store: a namespaced key that includes everything the value depends on (tenant, user, locale, version), a TTL on every entry, and a working path when the cache is down.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: On the server, computed or fetched data is cached in: The memory of each process
Cache in process memory only small, nearly static data, with a size bound and a TTL: each instance has its own copy, so never cache there what must be the same on every instance.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: On the server, computed or fetched data is cached in: Nothing
There is no server-side cache: do not add one unasked; fix the slow query or call first, and propose a cache together with its invalidation rule.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it

Cached values expire by TTL only: choose the TTL from how stale the value may be, add 10 to 20 % of random jitter so that keys do not expire together, and never cache what must be exact (permissions, balances).

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A cached value is refreshed by: Deleting the key when the data is written
Delete the cache key in the code path that writes the data, after the write is committed, and keep a TTL as a safety net; a new cached read comes with the list of writes that purge it.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A cached value is refreshed by: A version in the key
Put the data’s version in the cache key and bump it on write, so that stale entries are never read and simply expire; keep a TTL on every entry.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it

Keep the Dockerfile multi-stage, on a base image pinned to an exact version: install from the lockfile, copy only the build output and production dependencies into the last stage, run as a non-root user, and keep secrets out of every layer. Run one process per container, and do not let Node.js be PID 1 without an init process (`--init`, tini): it must receive `SIGTERM` and reap child processes.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The service is built into a container image: No: the platform builds or runs it
No container image is built here: do not add a Dockerfile or a Compose file unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it

Read configuration from environment variables only, through the one module that validates them at startup; never read `process.env` elsewhere, never hard-code a URL, a port or a credential, and add each new variable to the example env file.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: All configuration comes from environment variables, validated at startup.
Configuration lives in the project’s configuration files: follow them, and do not move settings to environment variables unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: On `SIGTERM`, the process finishes what is in flight before it exits.
Keep shutdown clean: on `SIGTERM`, stop accepting connections, finish in-flight requests and jobs within the grace period, then close pools and exit; register every new long-lived resource (server, worker, timer, connection) in that shutdown path.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: On `SIGTERM`, the process finishes what is in flight before it exits.
Do not add signal handling: the process may be stopped at any time, so keep every operation safe to interrupt and to run again.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The back end is: One application (a modular monolith)
The back end is one modular monolith: add code to the module that owns the domain, call another module only through its public interface, and never propose a new service or a message bus for what a function call does.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The back end is: Several services, each with its own data
Each service owns its data: never read or write another service’s tables, go through its API or its events, treat every such call as able to fail or time out, and do not add a new service unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The back end is: Functions run on demand (serverless)
Code runs as short-lived functions: keep startup light, create clients outside the handler, hold no state in memory between invocations, and hand to a queue any work that may pass the time limit.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A process keeps nothing in memory or on its disk that another instance would need.
Keep processes stateless: no session, counter, lock, scheduled timer or uploaded file in process memory or on the local disk that another instance would need; put shared state in the database, the shared cache or object storage.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A process keeps nothing in memory or on its disk that another instance would need.
A single instance runs, so state in process memory is acceptable; mark it with a comment so that it can be moved when a second instance is added.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Work that does not fit in a request runs on: A job queue (BullMQ, pg-boss…)
Slow work runs on the job queue: enqueue from the request with a small payload of ids, make each handler safe to run twice, set a number of attempts with backoff, and never do slow work in the request itself.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it

Work goes through the message broker: acknowledge a message only after its work is committed, make every consumer safe to run twice, and send repeated failures to a dead-letter queue instead of requeueing forever.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Work that does not fit in a request runs on: An event log (Kafka…)
Events go through a partitioned log: pick the key whose events must stay ordered, since order holds within a partition only, make consumers safe to replay, and change an event’s schema by adding fields only.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Work that does not fit in a request runs on: Nothing: everything runs in the request
There is no queue: do not add a broker or a job library unasked; keep work in the request short, and say when a change needs work that cannot fit in it.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Work that does not fit in a request runs on: Something else
Work outside the request runs on {value}: follow the existing producers and consumers, and make every handler safe to run twice.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Updates are pushed to clients with: Server-Sent Events
Push updates with Server-Sent Events: send an `id` with each event so that a client resumes with `Last-Event-ID`, send a heartbeat comment, free the listener when the connection closes, and do not add WebSockets for a one-way stream.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Updates are pushed to clients with: WebSockets
Push updates over the existing WebSocket layer: authenticate at the handshake, validate every incoming message, free listeners on close, and publish through the shared channel, not process memory, so that every instance reaches its clients.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Updates are pushed to clients with: Polling by the client
Clients poll for updates: keep the polled endpoint cheap (an ETag and 304, or a `since` parameter), and do not add Server-Sent Events or WebSockets unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Updates are pushed to clients with: Nothing: there is no live update
There is no live update channel: do not add Server-Sent Events, WebSockets or polling unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Webhooks: the back end Sends some to its users
Send a webhook from a background job, never inside the request: sign the payload, retry with backoff, and include an event id so that the receiver can ignore a duplicate.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Webhooks: the back end Receives some from other services
On an incoming webhook, verify the signature over the raw body before parsing it, answer 2xx fast and do the work in a job, and ignore an event id that was already handled.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Webhooks: the back end Neither sends nor receives any
The back end neither sends nor receives webhooks: do not add any unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Request rates are limited: In the application, with a shared counter
Rate limits live in the application, with counters in the shared store, never in process memory: put every new public or costly route (sign-in, password reset, search, export) behind the limiter, keyed by account or by IP, and answer 429 with `Retry-After`.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Request rates are limited: At the reverse proxy or the API gateway
Rate limits are set at the reverse proxy or the gateway: do not add a limiter in application code; say when a new route is costly or sensitive enough to need its own limit there.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Request rates are limited: Nowhere
No rate limit exists: do not add a limiter unasked, but say when a new route (sign-in, password reset, costly query) is open to abuse without one.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Under load, or when a dependency fails, the code: Retries with backoff, idempotent calls only
Retry a failed call to a dependency only when it is idempotent, with exponential backoff, jitter and a small cap on attempts; honor `Retry-After`, and never retry a 4xx other than 429.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Under load, or when a dependency fails, the code: Cuts calls to a failing dependency (circuit breaker)
Call unreliable dependencies through the project’s circuit breaker, with a short timeout, so that a slow dependency fails fast instead of holding connections; do not write a second breaker.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Under load, or when a dependency fails, the code: Bounds queues and concurrency, and refuses the rest
Bound everything that can pile up: a maximum length on queues and buffers, a concurrency limit on parallel work (no unbounded `Promise.all` over input-sized lists), a request body limit, and a 429 or 503 with `Retry-After` when full.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Under load, or when a dependency fails, the code: Serves a degraded answer rather than an error
When a secondary dependency fails, keep the main path working: serve the cached or partial answer and mark it as such, and never let an optional feature fail the whole request.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A performance change starts from a measurement, never from intuition.
Do not optimise by intuition: measure first (CPU profile, event loop lag, query plan, p99 latency rather than the average), change one thing, and report the numbers before and after.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A performance change starts from a measurement, never from intuition.
Write the faster version directly when the cost is obvious; a measurement is only needed before a change that makes the code harder to read.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Tests that touch the database run against: A real database (container or test instance)
Test database code against the real test database, never a mock: run the migrations, isolate each test (transaction rollback or truncation), and create the rows a test needs in the test itself.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Tests that touch the database run against: An in-memory substitute (SQLite, pg-mem…)
Tests run on an in-memory substitute of the database: keep queries within what it supports, and say when a query uses a feature only the real database has, since the tests cannot prove it.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Tests that touch the database run against: Mocks of the data layer
Tests mock the data layer: mock at the repository or service boundary, never the driver, and say that SQL and migrations are not covered when a change touches them.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Every new endpoint comes with a test that calls it over HTTP.
Give every new or changed endpoint a test that calls it over HTTP: the success case, an invalid input, a call without credentials and a call on another user’s resource, each checking the status code and the body.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Every new endpoint comes with a test that calls it over HTTP.
Test the services and business rules directly, in fast tests without network; do not add HTTP-level tests unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The service emits: Metrics
Instrument new endpoints, jobs and outbound calls with the existing metrics helpers (count, errors, duration as a histogram), and keep label values few and bounded: never a user id, an email or a raw URL as a label.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The service emits: Traces (OpenTelemetry…)
Let the existing tracing setup create spans: add one only around a significant unit of work, pass the context through queues and outbound calls, and never put a secret or personal data in an attribute.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The service emits: A request or trace id in every log line
Carry the request or trace id through every log line, job payload and outbound call of a request, with the existing context helper rather than a parameter threaded by hand.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The service emits: Health endpoints for the platform
Keep the liveness endpoint free of dependencies and let the readiness endpoint check the ones a request needs: wire any new required dependency into readiness, and keep both cheap and unauthenticated.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The service emits: None of these
The service has no metrics, traces or health endpoints: do not add an observability library unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it

Query: Responses and data are cached: Nowhere
Nothing is cached: do not add a cache at any level unless asked; fix the slow query or call first.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The application cache is filled: On a miss: read the cache, else the database, then fill (cache-aside)
Cache with cache-aside: read the cache, on a miss read the database and fill the cache with a TTL; protect a hot key against a stampede (a lock or one shared in-flight load, and jitter on the TTL).

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The application cache is filled: On every write, together with the database (write-through)
Cache with write-through: every write updates the database and the cache in the same code path, through the existing helper; never write one without the other, and give entries a TTL so unread data leaves.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The application cache is filled: First; the database is updated later (write-behind)
Writes land in the cache and reach the database later: use it only for data that tolerates a loss if the cache fails (counters, statistics), never for money, permissions or anything that must survive.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The application cache is filled: Ahead of expiry, for hot keys (refresh-ahead)
Hot keys are refreshed before they expire: register a new hot key in the existing refresh job instead of letting it expire under load, and only for keys that are read often and predictably.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The application cache is filled: There is no application cache
There is no application cache: do not add Redis, Memcached or an in-memory cache unless asked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When the data behind a cached entry changes, the entry: Stays until its TTL runs out
Cached entries expire by TTL only: choose a TTL as short as the staleness the feature tolerates, state it next to the key, and never cache without one.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When the data behind a cached entry changes, the entry: Is deleted by the code that writes
Every write deletes the cache entries built from the data it changes, after the database commit: when adding a cached read, add its invalidation to every write path in the same change, and keep a TTL as a safety net.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When the data behind a cached entry changes, the entry: Is left behind: the key carries a version
Cache keys carry a version of the data they hold: bump the version on write instead of deleting entries, build keys through the existing helper, and keep a TTL so old versions leave.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: An operation too slow for a request: Is queued; the API answers 202 with a status URL to poll
Slow work never runs inside a request: enqueue a job, answer `202 Accepted` with a `Location` header to a status resource, and let the worker update that status (pending, running, done, failed).

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: An operation too slow for a request: Is queued; the client is told when it ends (webhook, push)
Slow work never runs inside a request: enqueue a job, answer at once with its identifier, and notify the client through the existing callback or push channel when it ends, with its failure included.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: An operation too slow for a request: Runs inside the request anyway
Slow work runs inside the request: there is no job queue, so do not add one unless asked; set a timeout, and say so when an operation can exceed it.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When work arrives faster than it is processed: Queues are bounded: the system refuses early (429, 503)
Every queue and buffer is bounded: when one is full, refuse early with 429 or 503 and a `Retry-After` header; never add an unbounded queue, buffer or in-memory list of pending work.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When work arrives faster than it is processed: A queue absorbs the peak; workers keep a constant rate
A queue absorbs peaks and workers drain it at a rate the downstream service holds: do not raise worker concurrency to drain faster without checking that service, and still give the queue a maximum length and an alert on its depth.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When work arrives faster than it is processed: Nothing is planned
Nothing limits incoming work yet: do not add an unbounded queue or in-memory buffer, which only postpones the overload until memory runs out; say so when a change can receive bursts.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: On the queues of this system: A message can be delivered more than once
Delivery is at least once: make every consumer and job idempotent (a deduplication key, an upsert, a check of the current state) so that handling the same message twice changes nothing.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: On the queues of this system: Several workers consume the same queue
Several workers consume the same queue: a handler must be safe to run next to another copy of itself, keep no state in the worker between messages, and never assume two messages are handled in the order they were sent.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: On the queues of this system: A large payload goes to object storage; the message carries a reference
Never put a large payload in a message: store it in object storage and send only its reference; the consumer reads it from there and handles a missing object.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: On the queues of this system: Urgent work has its own queue or a priority
Urgent work has its own queue or priority: send a new job to the queue that matches its urgency, never raise a priority to hide a slow job, and check that low-priority work is still drained.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Between internal services, calls use: REST over HTTP
Internal services call each other with REST over HTTP: reuse the shared HTTP client with keep-alive and a timeout, follow the existing contract, and do not add gRPC or GraphQL between services.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Between internal services, calls use: gRPC
Internal services call each other with gRPC: change the `.proto` contract first, only by adding fields and never by reusing a field number, regenerate the stubs, and set a deadline on every call; do not add REST calls between services.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Between internal services, calls use: GraphQL
Internal services are reached through GraphQL: extend the existing schema, batch nested lookups to avoid one query per item, and keep the depth and cost limits on queries; do not add another protocol between services.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Between internal services, calls use: Messages only, no direct call
Services exchange messages only: never add a direct synchronous call from one service to another; publish an event or send a command on the existing broker.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Between internal services, calls use: There is only one service
There is a single service: do not add an internal RPC layer or a message broker to split it unless asked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it

Internal services talk with {value}; use it for every call between services and do not introduce another protocol.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Clients learn about a change on the server through: Server-Sent Events
Push server changes to clients with Server-Sent Events on the existing stream; do not add WebSocket or polling, and remember that an instance holds each open stream, so events must reach every instance.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Clients learn about a change on the server through: WebSocket
Push server changes to clients over the existing WebSocket connection; do not add another channel, handle reconnection, and publish events through the shared broker so every instance can deliver them.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Clients learn about a change on the server through: Polling
Clients poll for changes: keep the polled endpoint cheap and cacheable, give it a sensible interval with backoff, and do not add WebSocket or Server-Sent Events unless asked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Clients learn about a change on the server through: Nothing: they reload
There is no real-time channel: do not add WebSocket, Server-Sent Events or polling unless asked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Clients learn about a change on the server through: Something else
Clients learn about server changes through {value}; use it and do not add another real-time channel.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A performance change starts from a measurement, never from an intuition about the code.
Before optimising, name the metric that confirms the problem (a latency percentile, queries per request, database CPU), measure it under load, and measure again after the change; never add a cache to hide a chatty or oversized query.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A performance change starts from a measurement, never from an intuition about the code.
An obvious inefficiency may be fixed without a measurement; keep the fix small and say what it is expected to improve.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Under load, this system has to stay clear of: Many small network or SQL calls per request
Never issue one network or SQL call per item of a list: batch them, join, or fetch with one wider query, and count the calls a request makes when changing a read path.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Under load, this system has to stay clear of: Reading more rows or columns than needed
Select only the columns and rows a request uses: project, filter and paginate in the database, never in application code after loading everything.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Under load, this system has to stay clear of: A client or a connection pool created per request
Create HTTP clients, database pools and broker connections once and share them; never build one inside a request handler or a job.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Under load, this system has to stay clear of: Business logic running inside the database
Keep processing out of the database: no business logic or formatting in stored procedures, triggers or heavy SQL functions; the database stores and queries, the application computes.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Under load, this system has to stay clear of: Heavy work on the servers that answer requests
Keep heavy work (reports, image or file processing, bulk updates) off the servers that answer requests: hand it to a background worker through the queue.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Under load, this system has to stay clear of: Blocking I/O on a request path
Never block on I/O in a request path: use the asynchronous API of every file, network and database call, and never run a long CPU-bound loop on the thread or event loop that serves requests.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Several customers (tenants) share the system: Yes, each with quotas and rate limits
Tenants share the system under quotas: put every new endpoint, job or resource behind the existing per-tenant quota and rate limit, and never let work for one tenant use a pool, a queue or a lock that starves the others.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Several customers (tenants) share the system: Yes, without limits per tenant yet
Tenants share the system without limits per tenant: say so when a change lets one tenant consume a shared resource without bound (a list without a page size, a bulk job, a fan-out), and propose a quota rather than adding one unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Several customers (tenants) share the system: No
The system serves a single customer: do not add tenant identifiers, per-tenant quotas or tenant isolation unless asked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The health of an instance is checked by: Two probes: liveness and readiness
Liveness answers without calling the database or any other dependency; readiness checks only what the instance needs to take traffic. Never add a dependency check to liveness: a slow database would get every instance restarted.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The health of an instance is checked by: One health endpoint
One health endpoint is probed by the load balancer or the orchestrator: keep it fast and free of calls to slow dependencies, and do not add a check that can fail on every instance at once.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The health of an instance is checked by: Nothing
No health endpoint exists: do not add one unless asked, and say so when a change needs the platform to know that an instance is ready or stuck.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The system is monitored for: Performance: latency, throughput, errors, saturation
Instrument every new endpoint, job and outbound call with the existing metrics and traces: duration, outcome and count, with labels of bounded cardinality (never a user id or a raw URL).

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The system is monitored for: Availability, measured from outside against an objective (SLO)
Availability is measured by an external probe against an objective: keep the journey it exercises working when changing those endpoints, and say so when a change can spend the error budget (a migration, a restart, a new dependency).

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The system is monitored for: Security: failed sign-ins, unusual access, audit trail
Emit an audit event through the existing mechanism for every failed sign-in, refused permission and administrative action a change adds, with who, what and when, and no secret in it.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The system is monitored for: Usage: who uses what and how much (quotas, billing)
Record usage per account through the existing usage counters for every new feature that is billed or limited by a quota; never derive billing from application logs.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The system is monitored for: Nothing yet
There is no monitoring stack yet: do not add metrics, tracing or dashboards unless asked; keep logs useful enough to diagnose a failure.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: An alert fires on a symptom users feel and leads to one action.
When adding or changing an alert, alert on a symptom users feel (error rate, a latency percentile, availability against its objective), not on a cause; give it one action and a runbook, and never add an alert nobody has to act on.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: An alert fires on a symptom users feel and leads to one action.
Alerts and dashboards are managed outside this repository; do not add or change one, and say which signal a change would deserve.

Workflows are choreographed: publish an event that states a fact in the past tense and let each service react; carry a correlation id on every event, and propose a coordinator when a flow grows beyond 4 or 5 steps.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A workflow that spans several services or steps is driven by: A coordinator that calls each step and tracks the state (orchestration)
Workflows are orchestrated: add a step to the existing coordinator with its state, its retry and its failure path; never let a service trigger the next step on the side with an event or a direct call.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A workflow that spans several services or steps is driven by: Nothing: there is no such workflow
There is no workflow across services: do not add a workflow engine, a saga or an event bus unless asked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The order of messages is guaranteed: Per key (partition or message group)
Messages are ordered per key only: give every message about one entity the same partition or group key (its id), never rely on order across keys, and keep handlers fast since a slow message holds back its whole group.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The order of messages is guaranteed: Globally, by a single consumer
A single consumer keeps a global order: do not add a second consumer or parallel handling to that queue, and propose ordering per key when throughput becomes the problem.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The order of messages is guaranteed: Not at all
Message order is not guaranteed: never write a handler that depends on it; carry a version or a timestamp in the message and ignore one that is older than the state already applied.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Messaging also follows: Publish-subscribe: an event is published once for all its subscribers
A fact that interests several consumers is published once on its topic: add a subscriber instead of another direct call from the publisher, never make the publisher know its subscribers, and keep published event shapes backward compatible.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Messaging also follows: Pipes and filters: processing in independent stages linked by queues
Processing runs as independent stages linked by queues: add a stage rather than growing an existing one, keep each stage stateless and idempotent, and never share state between stages outside the message.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Messaging also follows: A scheduler, agents and a supervisor for long workflows with external systems
Long workflows with external systems go through the scheduler, its agents and the supervisor: add a step with its timeout, retry and compensation, and never call the external system outside an agent.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Messaging also follows: None of these
Messaging stays simple here: do not add topics, processing pipelines or a workflow supervisor unless asked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: To fit how data is read and written, the system uses: Separate write and read models (CQRS)
Writes go through commands on the write model and reads through the read model, which may be a little late: never write through a read model, never read your own write from it, and keep CQRS out of plain CRUD areas.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: To fit how data is read and written, the system uses: Event sourcing: the events are the source of truth
State is the projection of an append-only event log: never update or delete a stored event, never change the meaning of an event type; add a new versioned type and keep every old version readable by the projections.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: To fit how data is read and written, the system uses: Materialized views or precomputed tables
Expensive, frequent reads come from precomputed views: treat a view as late compared with its source, never write to it by hand, update its refresh or projection when the source shape changes, and keep a way to rebuild it from scratch.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: To fit how data is read and written, the system uses: Index tables kept next to a key-value store
Lookups on a non-key field go through an index table: update every index table in the same write path as the record it points to, and never scan the main store to search by another field.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: To fit how data is read and written, the system uses: None: one model, read and written
One model is read and written: do not introduce CQRS, event sourcing or materialized views unless asked; on simple CRUD they add complexity without gain.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A large upload or download goes: Straight to object storage, with a signed, short-lived URL
Large files move straight between the client and object storage with a pre-signed URL: sign one object path and one operation, valid 15 minutes or less; never sign a whole bucket or a long-lived URL, and never stream the bytes through the API.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A large upload or download goes: Through the API
Files go through the API: stream them to storage without buffering a whole file in memory, enforce a size limit at the boundary, and do not hand out direct storage URLs.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A large upload or download goes: Nowhere: there is none
The system handles no large file: do not add object storage or an upload path unless asked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: In front of the services, there is: An API gateway (routing, TLS, authentication)
An API gateway routes, ends TLS and authenticates: declare a new public route in its configuration, and never put a business rule or a decision in it; it routes and protects, the services decide.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: In front of the services, there is: A backend per kind of client (backends for frontends)
Each kind of client has its own backend: put aggregation and shaping for a screen in the backend of that client, keep business rules in the services behind, and never copy a rule into two of these backends.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: In front of the services, there is: A gateway, then a backend per kind of client
A gateway routes and authenticates, then a backend per kind of client aggregates for its screens: keep business rules in the services behind both, never in the gateway and never copied into two client backends.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: In front of the services, there is: Nothing: clients call the API directly
Clients call the API directly: do not add a gateway or a backend per client unless asked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: An older system lives next to this code: Yes, and it is replaced route by route behind a facade (strangler fig)
A legacy system is replaced route by route behind a facade: migrate one route at a time and switch it in the facade, never add a feature to the legacy side, and never propose a rewrite of everything at once.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: An older system lives next to this code: Yes, and it stays: a translation layer isolates its model
Reach the older or external system only through its translation layer: never let its names, types or status codes leak into the domain model, and map a new field in that layer.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: An older system lives next to this code: No
There is no legacy system to migrate: change working code in place and in small steps; do not propose a rewrite or add a facade unless asked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Outside the application code, the platform provides: A sidecar or mesh proxy for outgoing calls (retries, TLS, metrics)
A sidecar or mesh proxy handles retries, TLS and metrics of calls between services: do not add retries or TLS for those calls in application code, since two layers of retries multiply the load on a failing service.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Outside the application code, the platform provides: A sidecar or agent that ships logs and metrics
A sidecar or agent ships logs and metrics: write logs to standard output and expose metrics the existing way; never add a log shipper, a file appender or a vendor client to the application.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Outside the application code, the platform provides: An external configuration store, changed without a deployment
Configuration comes from the external configuration store and can change while the application runs: read a setting through the existing configuration client each time it is needed, never copy it into a constant or a file of the image.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Outside the application code, the platform provides: None of these
The platform provides no sidecar or configuration store: configuration is set at deployment, and the application handles its own TLS, retries and log output; do not add a service mesh unless asked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When a call to a dependency fails, the code: Retries with backoff, behind a circuit breaker
Wrap every call to a dependency in the existing retry and circuit breaker: retry only transient errors, with exponential backoff, jitter and a capped number of attempts, and fail fast while the breaker is open.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When a call to a dependency fails, the code: Retries with backoff, without a circuit breaker
Retry only transient errors, with exponential backoff, jitter and a small cap on attempts; never retry at once or without limit, and say so when a new call would need a circuit breaker, since retries alone finish off a failing dependency.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When a call to a dependency fails, the code: Does not retry: the failure goes back to the caller
Do not retry a failed call to a dependency in code: set a timeout, return the failure to the caller, and do not add a retry loop or a circuit breaker library unless asked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: An operation that changes several services or external systems is kept consistent by: Compensating actions that undo the steps already done
Give every step of a workflow across systems a compensating action, run compensations in reverse order when a later step fails, and make each one idempotent; a compensation is not a rollback, since other readers already saw the intermediate state.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: An operation that changes several services or external systems is kept consistent by: One database transaction: an operation never spans two systems
An operation changes one database inside one transaction: never call another service or an external system inside a transaction, and never split one business operation over two systems without asking.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: An operation that changes several services or external systems is kept consistent by: Nothing: a failure is repaired by hand
Nothing undoes a workflow that fails half-way: order the steps so the one most likely to fail runs first, log enough to repair by hand, and say so when a change adds a step that can leave data inconsistent.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The system also relies on: Separate pools per dependency or per client (bulkheads)
Pools are separated per dependency or per client so a failure stays local: give a new dependency its own bounded connection pool, concurrency limit and timeout, and never route its calls through a pool shared with another one.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The system also relies on: A leader elected among the instances for work that runs once
Work that must run once goes through the existing leader election: pass the fencing token (the term number) with every write the leader makes, and never assume the instance is still leader after a pause.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The system also relies on: Independent copies of the whole stack, one per group of customers (stamps, cells)
The stack is deployed as independent stamps, each serving a group of customers: never add a call, a shared database or shared state between two stamps, and keep every change deployable one stamp at a time.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The system also relies on: Identical back ends in several regions, each able to serve anyone
Any region can serve any user: never keep data or state that exists in one region only, never assume two requests of a user reach the same region, and say how a new kind of data is replicated.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The system also relies on: Sign-in delegated to an identity provider (OIDC, SAML)
Sign-in is delegated to an identity provider: never store or check a password here, validate the signature, issuer, audience and expiry of every token, and map provider roles to local permissions in one place.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The system also relies on: A dedicated host that validates requests before the trusted services (gatekeeper)
A gatekeeper validates and filters every public request before the trusted services: never expose an internal service around it, keep it free of business logic and of credentials to the data, and still validate inputs in the services.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A name says the intent in full words, even when it gets long.
Name every function, variable and type after its intent, in full words (`startInstance(instance)`, not `proc(d, f)`); when a comment is needed to say what a name means, rename instead.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A name says the intent in full words, even when it gets long.
Keep names short and follow the abbreviations the code base already uses; do not rename existing identifiers to longer ones as a side effect.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: I prefer short functions with one responsibility to long ones read top to bottom.
Keep a function to one responsibility, readable on one screen and at a cyclomatic complexity of 10 at most: return early with guard clauses instead of nesting branches. Do not pass a boolean flag or `null` to switch a function’s behaviour: write two functions or take an options object.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: I prefer short functions with one responsibility to long ones read top to bottom.
Keep a linear procedure in one function rather than a chain of two-line functions that call each other; extract a function only when it is reused or hides a real detail.
