Refactor code the task touches in small steps that each keep the tests green; when no test covers it, write the test first, and keep the refactor apart from the behaviour change.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When code next to the task deserves a refactor, the assistant: Tells me, and leaves it for a separate change
Do not refactor code next to the task: say what deserves it and why at the end, and leave it for a separate change.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When code next to the task deserves a refactor, the assistant: Leaves it alone
Do not refactor or restyle code the task does not require changing, even when it looks improvable.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The code is mostly written: With classes and objects
Write new behaviour as methods on the class that owns the data, next to the existing classes; do not add a module of free functions that works on another class’s state.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The code is mostly written: With functions and plain data
Write functions over plain data and compose them (`map`, `filter`, `reduce`); do not introduce a class where a function and a type are enough, and share no mutable state between functions.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The code is mostly written: Both: objects at the boundaries, functions for calculations
Use objects behind an interface where an implementation can be swapped (providers, storage, plugins), and pure functions over plain data for calculations and transformations.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The code is mostly written: Something else
The code is written in this style: {value}; follow it in new code and do not mix in another one.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Data is immutable by default: a new value is created rather than changing one in place.
Never mutate an argument or a shared value: return a new one, and declare data read-only (`const`, `readonly`); mutate in place only inside a hot loop where the copy was measured as a cost.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Data is immutable by default: a new value is created rather than changing one in place.
Changing a local value in place is fine; never mutate an argument the caller still uses without the function name saying so.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Business calculations are pure functions; I/O, the clock and randomness stay at the edges.
Write a business calculation as a pure function of its arguments: read the data before calling it and write the result after, never inside it. Pass the current time, random values and generated ids in as parameters: a function that reads `Date.now()` or a global is not pure and cannot be tested without a mock.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Business calculations are pure functions; I/O, the clock and randomness stay at the edges.
Business code may read the clock and do I/O where it needs it; do not restructure it into pure functions unasked, and keep a way to fake the clock and the I/O in tests.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: To share behaviour between classes, the code uses: Composition and interfaces, no inheritance of our own
Never extend one of the project’s classes to reuse its code: pass the behaviour in as a collaborator behind an interface. Extending a class the framework requires is fine.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: To share behaviour between classes, the code uses: Inheritance only for a true “is a” relation
Extend a class only when the subclass can replace its parent everywhere without surprise; to reuse code, compose. Keep hierarchies one level deep.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: To share behaviour between classes, the code uses: Base classes that hold the common code
Put code shared by sibling classes in their existing base class and leave the steps that differ abstract; do not add a level to the hierarchy unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Everything is private unless it has to be public: fields, methods, exports.
Expose the minimum: private fields, no getter or setter added by default, and export only what another module uses; state changes through a method that keeps the object valid. In TypeScript, `private` is only checked at compile time: use a `#field` when a value must stay private at run time.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Everything is private unless it has to be public: fields, methods, exports.
Plain objects with public fields are fine; do not wrap them in classes with getters and setters, and do not narrow existing visibility as a side effect.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: An abstraction (interface, generic parameter, option) is added: When a second real case exists
Write the concrete code first; add an interface, a generic parameter or an option only when a second real case exists, never for a hypothetical one.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: An abstraction (interface, generic parameter, option) is added: At the third case
Write the concrete code, and tolerate a second similar case; abstract at the third one, once what really varies is visible.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: An abstraction (interface, generic parameter, option) is added: Up front, where variation is expected
Where the task names a point that will vary (provider, format, policy), isolate it behind an interface from the start, so that a new case is a new implementation and not an edited `switch`.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: I prefer a little duplication to the wrong abstraction.
Merge two pieces of code only when they state the same business knowledge and will change for the same reason; code that looks alike by chance stays duplicated.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: I prefer a little duplication to the wrong abstraction.
Do not repeat logic: before writing a helper, search for an existing one, and extract a shared function as soon as the same logic appears twice.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The assistant holds new code to: Single responsibility: one reason to change
Give a class or module one reason to change: do not add billing, notification or another actor’s concern to a service that does something else; create or use the module that owns it.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The assistant holds new code to: Open/closed: extend without editing
When a new case would mean editing a `switch` or an `if` chain on a type in several places, add an implementation of the existing interface instead.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The assistant holds new code to: Interface segregation: small interfaces per client
Keep an interface to the methods its caller uses: split one that forces an implementation to stub methods, and depend on the narrowest one.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The assistant holds new code to: Dependency inversion: depend on abstractions
Business code depends on an interface it defines, and the detail implements it; this is about the direction of imports, so a dependency injection container alone does not satisfy it.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The assistant holds new code to: Law of Demeter: talk to direct neighbours only
Do not chain through an object’s internals (`a.getB().getC().run()`): call a method on the direct collaborator and let it delegate.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The assistant holds new code to: Tell, don’t ask
Ask an object to act rather than reading its state to decide in its place: move the condition into a method of the object that owns the data.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A design pattern is used only when its problem is really there; a function or a plain object comes first.
Before introducing a design pattern, state the problem it solves here and what it costs; with a single variant, write the direct code. Prefer a function or an object literal to a Strategy or Factory class hierarchy, and a wrapper function to a Decorator class, when the language allows it.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A design pattern is used only when its problem is really there; a function or a plain object comes first.
Use the named patterns the code base already uses (Factory, Builder, Strategy, Adapter, Decorator) and name the classes after them, so that the structure is recognized at a glance.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A shared resource (configuration, connection pool, client) reaches the code that uses it: Through constructor or function parameters
Pass a shared resource in through the constructor or the function parameters and create it once at the entry point; never write a Singleton class or reach for a global.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A shared resource (configuration, connection pool, client) reaches the code that uses it: Through a dependency injection container
Register a shared resource in the dependency injection container and receive it by injection; never instantiate it inside the class that uses it, and never write a Singleton class.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A shared resource (configuration, connection pool, client) reaches the code that uses it: By importing a module-level instance
Import the existing module-level instance of a shared resource; never create a second one, and keep a way to replace it in tests.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Source folders are organized: By domain or use case (`billing/`, `instances/`)
Put a new file in the folder of the domain or use case it serves, next to what changes with it; do not create top-level folders named after a technical type (`controllers/`, `utils/`).

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Source folders are organized: By technical type (`controllers/`, `services/`, `models/`)
Put a new file in the existing folder of its technical type (`controllers/`, `services/`, `models/`) and name it after its domain; do not start a per-domain folder next to them.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Source folders are organized: Another way
Source folders are organized this way: {value}; place new files accordingly and do not start another layout.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Business code never imports the framework, the ORM or a provider’s client.
Entities and use cases import nothing from the framework, the ORM, HTTP or a provider’s SDK: to reach one, declare an interface in the business code and implement it in an adapter. Keep business entities apart from ORM models and table shapes, so that the database schema does not dictate the business model.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Business code never imports the framework, the ORM or a provider’s client.
Business code may use the framework and the ORM directly; do not add interfaces and mapping layers to hide them, except in front of a detail that is likely to be replaced.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A module imports from another module: Only through its public entry point
Import from another module only through its public entry point, never from its internal files; when what you need is not exported, export it there on purpose or ask.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A module imports from another module: From any file, as long as there is no cycle
A module may import any file of another one, but never add an import that closes a cycle between two modules.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A module imports from another module: No rule
No import rule is enforced between modules; follow the imports the neighbouring files use and avoid adding a dependency between two modules that do not know each other yet.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Inside the code base, the structure is: Layers (presentation, application, domain, data)
The code is layered (presentation, application, domain, data): a layer calls only the one below it, never upward or across, and business rules go in the domain layer. Do not add a layer or a class that only forwards calls to the next one.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Inside the code base, the structure is: Hexagonal or clean: a domain core, ports and adapters
The code is hexagonal: dependencies point toward the domain. Use cases declare ports, adapters (controllers, repositories, clients) implement them, and the domain names no outer layer.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Inside the code base, the structure is: Feature modules, each with its own internals
The code is split into feature modules: a feature keeps its handlers, logic and data access together; put a change in the module that owns the behaviour and share only through its public interface.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Inside the code base, the structure is: The framework’s default (MVC or similar)
The code follows the framework’s default structure: put each file where the framework expects it and do not add layers of your own on top.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Inside the code base, the structure is: Something else
The code base is structured this way: {value}; place new code accordingly and do not introduce another structure.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When something happens that other parts of the code react to: The code calls them directly
Parts of the code call each other directly, so the flow can be read from the caller; do not introduce an event bus, an emitter or an observer unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When something happens that other parts of the code react to: It publishes an event that subscribers handle
Publish an event named in the past tense for a fact others react to, and add a subscriber instead of a direct call; the publisher never knows its subscribers. Write every event handler so that a duplicate or out-of-order event does no harm, carry a correlation id on each event and log it, and unsubscribe what you subscribe.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The code base uses: CQRS: separate read and write models
Reads and writes use separate models: a command changes state through the write model and returns no data, a query reads the read model and changes nothing; expect the read side to lag.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The code base uses: Event sourcing: state rebuilt from stored events
State is rebuilt from stored events: never edit or delete a stored event, change state only by appending one, and give a changed event shape a new version that old events are upgraded to.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The code base uses: A small core extended by plugins
Add a feature as a plugin against the existing plugin contract, not in the core; treat that contract as public and never change it without asking.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The code base uses: Functions run on demand (serverless)
Handlers run as on-demand functions: keep them short and stateless between calls, do the expensive setup outside the handler, and move work that may exceed the time limit elsewhere.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The code base uses: None of these
Do not introduce CQRS, event sourcing, a plugin system or on-demand functions unasked: one model serves reads and writes, and state is stored as it is.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The logic of a business action lives in: One use case per action (`StartInstance`)
Write each business action as its own use case that loads, calls the domain and saves, testable without the framework; a controller only validates, calls it and translates the result.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The logic of a business action lives in: A service per resource (`InstanceService`)
Put the logic of a business action in a method of the service that owns the resource; a controller only validates, calls it and translates the result into a response.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The logic of a business action lives in: The handler itself, one procedure per action
Write a business action as one procedure in its handler that reads, decides and writes; move a rule to a shared function once a second handler needs it, never copy it.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Domain-Driven Design building blocks (entities, value objects, aggregates) are used: In the complex core of the business only
Model the complex core of the business with entities, value objects and aggregates; write simple create-read-update-delete and configuration code plainly, without them. Make a value object immutable and compared by value, validated when built (`Money`, `Region`); an entity is compared by identity.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Domain-Driven Design building blocks (entities, value objects, aggregates) are used: Everywhere
Model every business concept as an entity (has an identity) or a value object (defined by its values), and change an aggregate only through its root, one aggregate per transaction. Make a value object immutable and compared by value, validated when built (`Money`, `Region`); an entity is compared by identity.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Domain-Driven Design building blocks (entities, value objects, aggregates) are used: Not used
Do not introduce Domain-Driven Design building blocks (aggregates, value object classes, domain events) unasked: follow the data structures the code already uses.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A business object carries its own rules and refuses an invalid change itself.
Put a business rule in a method of the entity it protects (`instance.stop(now)` throws on a forbidden transition); never set a status or a field from outside and never add a public setter for it.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A business object carries its own rules and refuses an invalid change itself.
Entities are plain data and the rules live in services: put a rule in the service that owns the action, in one place, and do not add behaviour to the data types.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The code uses the words of the business: when a concept is renamed, the code is renamed.
Name types, functions and tables with the exact words the business uses, one word per concept and no synonym; when a term in the task matches no name in the code, ask instead of inventing one. The same word can mean different things in two contexts (an instance for provisioning, an instance for billing): keep one model per context and translate between them, never share one type.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The code uses the words of the business: when a concept is renamed, the code is renamed.
Keep the names the code already has, even when the business now uses another word; do not rename identifiers to follow vocabulary unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Business code loads and saves its objects through: Repositories that hide the ORM or the SQL
Load and save business objects through a repository (`findById`, `save`) that returns domain objects, never ORM rows or query builders; add the method you need to the existing repository.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Business code loads and saves its objects through: Models that save themselves (Active Record)
Models load and save themselves: use their own query and save methods and do not wrap them in repository classes.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Business code loads and saves its objects through: The ORM or database client, called directly
Call the ORM or the database client directly where the data is needed; do not add a repository layer that only forwards to it.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: What crosses the API is a dedicated shape, never a database model or an entity as is.
Never return or accept a database model or an entity as is: map it to a flat transfer shape that lists each exposed field, so that an internal field never leaks and a schema change never changes the contract.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: What crosses the API is a dedicated shape, never a database model or an entity as is.
Models may be returned as they are, without a mapping layer; before exposing one, check that it holds no internal or sensitive field and hide those explicitly.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A method either changes state or returns a value, never both.
Write a method as a command that changes state and returns nothing beyond an id or a status, or as a query that returns a value and changes nothing; a `get…` or `find…` never writes.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A method either changes state or returns a value, never both.
A method may change state and return the result; still, never hide a write behind a name that reads (`get…`, `find…`, `is…`).

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A rule, a regular expression or a database query is preferred to a model call whenever it does the job.
Before adding a model call, check whether a rule, a regular expression or a database query does the job; call a model only where they cannot, and say why in the change.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A rule, a regular expression or a database query is preferred to a model call whenever it does the job.
A model call is acceptable where it saves code; still use deterministic code for anything with one exact answer (parsing, arithmetic, lookups, permission checks).

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A new model feature starts with a success criterion and evaluation cases, before its prompt.
Before writing the prompt of a new model feature, write down the task, its success criterion and a first set of evaluation cases; a prompt that works on three examples proves nothing.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A new model feature starts with a success criterion and evaluation cases, before its prompt.
A new model feature may start as a prototype (model and prompt); add evaluation cases before it reaches users, and say when a feature has none.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Before a call, the size of the input in tokens is: Counted with the tokenizer and checked against a budget
Count the input tokens of a call with the tokenizer helper the project uses and compare them to the budget of that call before sending; trim or refuse an input that exceeds it instead of letting the provider reject it.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Before a call, the size of the input in tokens is: Estimated from the character count
Estimate the input size of a call at about 4 characters per token (fewer for non-English text) and keep a margin under the context window, which holds the prompt and the answer together.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Before a call, the size of the input in tokens is: Not checked
Input size is not checked before a call: bound every user-supplied text with a maximum length, and handle the context-length error of the provider as an expected case.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: What the model remembers from one call to the next comes from: A conversation stored on our server
The conversation is stored on the server: rebuild the messages of each call from that store, scoped to the signed-in user, and never accept system instructions or past assistant turns from the client.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: What the model remembers from one call to the next comes from: The history the client sends with each request
The client sends the history with each request: treat all of it as untrusted input, validate its roles and size, and add the system instructions on the server only.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: What the model remembers from one call to the next comes from: Nothing: each call stands alone
Each model call stands alone: put everything the call needs in its own input, and do not add conversation storage unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Model identifiers are written: In one configuration module, by task
Model identifiers live in one configuration module, keyed by task: reference that entry at the call site and never write a model identifier as a string literal anywhere else.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Model identifiers are written: In environment variables
Model identifiers come from environment variables: read them through the configuration layer, document a new variable in the example environment file, and never hard-code a model identifier.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Model identifiers are written: Next to each call
Model identifiers are written next to each call, as a named constant: keep the exact, dated identifier and do not use a floating alias that changes model without a code change.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Model identifiers are written: Somewhere else
Model identifiers are configured here: {value}; never write one anywhere else.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Code that needs a model calls: Our own interface, which hides the provider
Call a model only through the project interface that hides the provider: never import the SDK of a provider outside the module that implements it, and keep provider-specific types out of feature code.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Code that needs a model calls: A provider-agnostic library
Call a model through the provider-agnostic library the project already uses; do not import the SDK of a provider directly, and do not rely on an option only one provider supports without saying so.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Code that needs a model calls: The provider’s SDK directly
The project calls the SDK of the model provider directly: keep those calls in the existing client module, and do not add a second provider or an abstraction layer unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Which model handles a task: One model for everything
One model serves every task: use the configured one for a new call and do not introduce a second model unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Which model handles a task: A model chosen per task (small, large, reasoning)
Each task has its own model: for a new task, pick the smallest configured model that passes its evaluation cases, and keep a reasoning model for hard multi-step tasks since it is slower and costs more.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Which model handles a task: A small model by default, a larger one for hard cases
Send a task to the small default model first and escalate to the larger one only through the existing routing rule; never call the larger model directly from feature code.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Sampling parameters (temperature, top-p, penalties) are set: Per task, in configuration next to the model
Sampling parameters are set per task in configuration, next to the model: add or change them there, never inline at a call site.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Sampling parameters (temperature, top-p, penalties) are set: At each call
Set sampling parameters explicitly at each call: temperature 0 to 0.2 for extraction, classification, JSON, code and SQL; 0.5 to 0.8 for conversation; higher only for drafting and ideas.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Sampling parameters (temperature, top-p, penalties) are set: Nowhere: the provider’s defaults apply
Leave sampling parameters at the defaults of the provider; when a task needs a predictable output, say so and propose a temperature instead of setting one silently.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Every call sets a maximum output length and checks why the model stopped.
Set an explicit maximum output length on every model call, sized for the task, and check the stop reason: an answer cut by the limit is an error to handle, never a JSON document to parse or a text to show as complete.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Every call sets a maximum output length and checks why the model stopped.
Leave the output length at its default unless the provider requires one; still check the stop reason before parsing a structured answer, since a truncated one is invalid.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Embeddings are stored in: PostgreSQL with pgvector
Embeddings live in PostgreSQL with pgvector: add a vector column through a migration with its approximate index (HNSW or IVFFlat), and combine similarity with ordinary SQL filters and joins in one query; do not add another vector store.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Embeddings are stored in: Qdrant
Embeddings live in Qdrant: reach it through the existing client module, store the filterable fields in the payload with their indexes, and do not add another vector store.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Embeddings are stored in: Weaviate
Embeddings live in Weaviate: reach it through the existing client module, declare a new property in the collection schema before using it as a filter, and do not add another vector store.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Embeddings are stored in: Chroma
Embeddings live in Chroma: reach it through the existing client module, store filterable fields as metadata, and do not add another vector store.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Embeddings are stored in: LanceDB
Embeddings live in LanceDB: reach it through the existing module, keep filterable fields as columns of the table, and do not add another vector store.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Embeddings are stored in: An in-memory FAISS index
Embeddings are searched in an in-memory FAISS index, which is a library and not a database: keep the code that rebuilds and persists it working, and keep the mapping from vector position to record and its metadata in the main database.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it

Embeddings are stored in {value}; reach it through the existing module and do not add another vector store.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it

Ask before changing the embedding model or its dimension: every stored vector has to be computed again, so say how many records that is.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
