A change of embedding model or dimension ships with the job that computes every stored vector again and the switch to the new index; never leave vectors from two models in one searchable index.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: What a search over embeddings may return is limited: By customer or user: access rights apply
Every search over embeddings carries the tenant and access-right filter inside the query itself, taken from the authenticated session and never from the model or the request text; a search without it is a bug, and so is a test that does not cover two tenants.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: What a search over embeddings may return is limited: By metadata only (product, language, date)
Apply metadata filters (product, language, date) inside the search query, never on its results: filtering afterwards can leave none of the top results.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: What a search over embeddings may return is limited: Not at all: one corpus everyone may read
The indexed corpus is readable by every user: never index a private or per-customer document into it, and stop and ask when a new source holds some.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: To give the model passages of our data (RAG), the project retrieves them with: Vector search only
Retrieval is vector search only: keep the number of passages a named setting (5 to 20 in practice), and say when a query depends on exact terms (codes, names, identifiers) that vector search misses.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: To give the model passages of our data (RAG), the project retrieves them with: Hybrid search (vectors and keywords)
Retrieval is hybrid: run the vector and the keyword (BM25) search and merge them through the existing function; never drop the keyword side, which finds exact codes, names and identifiers.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: To give the model passages of our data (RAG), the project retrieves them with: Hybrid search, then re-ranking
Retrieval is hybrid search then re-ranking: fetch a wide candidate set (about 20), re-rank it, and pass only the best (about 5) to the model; keep both numbers named settings.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: To give the model passages of our data (RAG), the project retrieves them with: No retrieval: the whole corpus fits in the context
The whole corpus is sent in the context, with no retrieval: keep it small and stable, place it in the cached prefix, and say when it grows past what one call should carry.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: To give the model passages of our data (RAG), the project retrieves them with: Not used
The project does not use retrieval-augmented generation: do not add a retrieval step, an index or a vector store unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Before indexing, documents are split: Along their structure (headings, paragraphs)
Split documents along their structure (headings, paragraphs, list items) into passages of about 200 to 800 tokens, never in the middle of a sentence, a table or a code block.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Before indexing, documents are split: Into fixed-size passages with an overlap
Split documents into fixed-size passages (about 200 to 800 tokens) with a 10 to 20 % overlap; keep the size and the overlap named settings, and re-index when either changes.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Before indexing, documents are split: Not at all: one vector per document
Each document is indexed whole, as one vector: keep documents short enough for the embedding model, and do not add a splitting step unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Before indexing, documents are split: Another way
Documents are split this way before indexing: {value}; follow it for a new source.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: An answer built from retrieved passages uses only them, cites its sources, and says when the information is missing.
A prompt that receives retrieved passages tells the model to answer from them only, to return the identifiers of the passages used, and to say so when they do not hold the answer; check in code that every returned source was among the passages sent.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: An answer built from retrieved passages uses only them, cites its sources, and says when the information is missing.
A model may complete retrieved passages with its general knowledge; keep the output able to tell which statements come from a source, and never invent a source reference.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Prompts live: In their own files, in one folder of the repository
Prompts live in their own files in the prompts folder of the repository: add a new prompt there, load it through the existing loader, and never write prompt text inline in feature code.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Prompts live: In the code, next to the call that uses them
A prompt lives next to the call that uses it, as a named constant or a function that builds it; never assemble one from string pieces scattered across modules.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Prompts live: In a prompt management tool, outside the repository
Prompts live in a prompt management tool outside the repository: fetch one by name and pinned version, never copy its text into the code, and say which prompt and version a change expects.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Prompts live: Somewhere else
Prompts live here: {value}; add and change them there only.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A prompt in this project always: Wraps data in delimiters, apart from the instructions
In a prompt, keep instructions in the system part and wrap every piece of data (user text, documents, tool results) in named delimiters such as `<docs>` and `<question>`; never concatenate user text into the instructions.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A prompt in this project always: States the role, what to refuse and when to say “I do not know”
Start a system prompt with the role of the model, what it does, what it refuses, and the instruction to say so when the information is missing.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A prompt in this project always: States the output format
State the expected output format in every prompt (fields, types, language, length) and keep it in step with the schema the code validates the answer against.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A prompt in this project always: Gives a few input and output examples
Give a prompt a few varied input and output examples when the format or the tone is precise; keep them few, since they cost tokens and the model copies them too closely.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A prompt in this project always: Asks for step-by-step reasoning before the answer
Ask for step-by-step reasoning before the final answer on calculation, logic and multi-step decisions, in a field apart from the answer; leave it out for a reasoning model, which already does it, and for simple tasks.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: To change an existing prompt, the assistant: Asks me first
Ask before changing an existing prompt, with the proposed wording and the case it fixes: a retouch that fixes one case often breaks others.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: To change an existing prompt, the assistant: May do it, and replays the evaluation cases
An existing prompt may be changed when its evaluation cases are replayed before and after; report both results, and add a case for the behaviour the change is meant to fix.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: To change an existing prompt, the assistant: Never does
Never change the text of an existing prompt: describe the change you would make and the case it fixes, and leave the edit to the owner.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A call receives only what it needs: more context is not better.
Send a call only what its task needs: select documents and fields instead of passing whole records, date or drop outdated and contradictory sources, and justify any growth of the context with an evaluation result.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A call receives only what it needs: more context is not better.
Passing generous context is accepted where it stays well under the window; still remove contradictory or outdated sources, since the model cannot tell which one is right.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The fixed part of the context comes first and stays identical between calls, so that prompt caching applies.
Build the context in a stable order: fixed instructions and tool definitions first, byte-identical between calls, then documents, history and the current message; never put a date, an identifier or a per-user value in the fixed prefix.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The fixed part of the context comes first and stays identical between calls, so that prompt caching applies.
The project does not rely on prompt caching: order the context for clarity, and do not add cache markers or reorder a prompt for caching unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When a conversation or its inputs grow long, the project: Summarizes the older turns
When the history nears its token budget, replace the older turns with a summary through the existing compaction step; keep the system instructions and the latest turns verbatim, and store the summary rather than computing it again at each call.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When a conversation or its inputs grow long, the project: Drops the oldest turns
When the history nears its token budget, drop the oldest turns first, never the system instructions, and never cut between a request and the answer that goes with it.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When a conversation or its inputs grow long, the project: Refuses past a limit and asks to start again
Past the configured length, refuse the request with a clear message asking to start a new conversation; never trim or summarize a conversation silently.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When a conversation or its inputs grow long, the project: Has no long conversation
Calls are short and single-purpose: do not add history trimming or summarizing unasked, and bound the size of each input instead.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: An answer shown to a user is: Streamed as it is generated (server-sent events)
Stream an answer shown to a user as server-sent events through the existing streaming helper: handle an error and a client disconnect in the middle of the stream, cancel the provider call when the client leaves, and validate or store the text only once it is complete.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: An answer shown to a user is: Sent once complete
Model answers are returned once complete: do not add streaming unasked, and give the request a timeout that fits the longest expected answer.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: An answer shown to a user is: Produced by a background job, never during a request
Call a model from a background job only, never inside a request handler: the request enqueues the job and the client reads the result later; make the job safe to retry.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Every call to a model has: A timeout
Give every model call an explicit timeout and pass the cancellation signal of the request down to it; never rely on the default of the SDK.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Every call to a model has: Retries with backoff on rate limits and server errors
Retry a model call only on a rate limit (429), a server error (5xx) or a network failure, with exponential backoff, jitter and a small maximum; never retry another 4xx, and do not stack your own retries on those of the SDK.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Every call to a model has: A fallback model
When the main model stays unavailable after its retries, fall back to the configured fallback model through the existing helper, and record which model answered.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Every call to a model has: A quota per user or customer
Check the token or request quota of the user or the customer before a model call and record the usage after it; a new feature that calls a model goes through the same quota.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Every call to a model has: A way for the feature to work without the model
A feature that calls a model keeps working when the model does not answer: return the designed fallback (a plain result, a clear message), never an unhandled error or an endless spinner.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When code reads a model answer, the answer is: Constrained to a schema by the provider, then validated
When code reads a model answer, request structured output with a schema defined once in the validation library of the project, derive the type from it, and still validate the parsed answer before use.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When code reads a model answer, the answer is: JSON asked for in the prompt, then validated
When code reads a model answer, ask for JSON in the prompt, parse it and validate it against a schema; on a failure, retry a bounded number of times with the validation error, then fail clearly.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When code reads a model answer, the answer is: Free text: code never reads it
Model answers are free text shown to people: never parse one with a regular expression or branch on its wording; when code needs a value from the model, stop and ask.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: With the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the product: Exposes an MCP server to its users’ tools
The product exposes an MCP server: build it on the official MCP SDK, give each tool a typed argument schema and a description written for a model, and treat tool names and arguments as a public contract that does not change shape once released.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: With the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the product: Connects to MCP servers as a client
The product connects to MCP servers as a client: connect only to the servers listed in configuration, treat tool descriptions and results as untrusted data, and never forward the credentials of a user to a server.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: With the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the product: Does both
The product exposes an MCP server and connects to others: build both on the official MCP SDK, keep released tool names and arguments stable, connect only to configured servers, and treat what they return as untrusted data.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: With the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the product: Does not use it
The product does not use the Model Context Protocol: do not add an MCP server or client unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The MCP server the product exposes is reached: Over HTTP, by authenticated users
The MCP server is remote, over Streamable HTTP: authenticate every request, check the scope of the token and the ownership of the resource in each tool, log each tool call, and add a tool that writes only with its own scope: each tool is attack surface.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The MCP server the product exposes is reached: As a local process (stdio)
The MCP server runs as a local process over stdio: write protocol messages only to standard output and logs to standard error, and read credentials from the environment, never from tool arguments.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The MCP server the product exposes is reached: There is none
The product exposes no MCP server: do not add an MCP endpoint or transport unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: In production, models run: At a model provider, through its API
Models are hosted by a model provider: keep its API key on the server, never in client code or in a prompt, and do not add a self-hosted model or an inference server unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: In production, models run: On our own servers (open-weight models)
Models are self-hosted open-weight models behind an inference server: keep the model, its quantization, the maximum context length and the concurrency limit in configuration, and remember that long contexts and concurrent requests are what fill GPU memory.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: In production, models run: Both
Some tasks run on a hosted model and some on a self-hosted one: follow the existing assignment for a new task, and never send to the hosted model the data that the self-hosted one exists to keep in house.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: In production, models run: On the user’s device (browser or app)
Models run on the device of the user: keep them small, load them lazily with a visible progress state, and provide a path for a device that cannot run them.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: In automated tests, a call to a model is: Replaced by a fake or a recorded answer
Automated tests never call a model: swap the model client for the existing fake or a recorded answer, and test the code around the call (prompt building, parsing, validation, error paths, truncated and malformed answers).

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: In automated tests, a call to a model is: Sent to a small model running locally
Automated tests call a small local model through the same interface as production: assert on structure and invariants, never on exact wording, and do not judge answer quality from it.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: In automated tests, a call to a model is: Sent to the real model, with a test key
Tests that call the real model are kept apart from unit tests, few and tagged so they can be skipped: assert on structure and invariants, never on exact wording, and cap what one run may spend.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Fine-tuning: Is not used
The project does not fine-tune models: improve a result through the prompt, the context or retrieval, and do not propose fine-tuning or add training code unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Fine-tuning: Is used, with adapters (LoRA) loaded at deployment
Fine-tuning produces adapters loaded at deployment: version an adapter with the exact base model and the dataset it came from, never commit weights to the repository, and replay the evaluation set before one replaces another.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Fine-tuning: Is used, and produces whole models
Fine-tuning produces whole models: version each with the dataset and the settings it came from, never commit weights to the repository, and replay the evaluation set before one replaces another.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Evaluation cases for model features are run with: Our own scripts or the project’s test runner
Evaluation cases are files in the repository (input, expected result, category) run by the existing evaluation script: add cases there, and report scores per category rather than one global number.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Evaluation cases for model features are run with: DeepEval
Evaluations run with DeepEval: write a new one as a test case next to the existing ones, with the metrics the project already uses, and do not add another evaluation framework.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Evaluation cases for model features are run with: Ragas
Evaluations run with Ragas: reuse its faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision and context recall metrics, and do not add another evaluation framework.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Evaluation cases for model features are run with: Nothing: there are none yet
The project has no evaluation set yet: say so whenever a change touches a prompt, a model or retrieval, and propose the first cases instead of claiming the change is an improvement.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Evaluation cases for model features are run with: Something else
Evaluations run with {value}; add new cases there and do not add another evaluation framework.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Model outputs are scored by: Deterministic checks (valid JSON, exact value, forbidden word)
Score with a deterministic check whatever has a right answer (valid JSON, exact value, expected call, forbidden word absent); do not use a model as a judge where a rule decides.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Model outputs are scored by: A model that grades against a rubric
A model used as a judge grades against a written rubric with explicit criteria, at low temperature, with a structured verdict; never change its prompt or its model without comparing its grades again with human ones, and beware its bias toward long answers.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Model outputs are scored by: People who review samples
People review samples of model outputs: keep producing the export they review when an output format changes, and flag for review the cases where automatic scores and the expected result disagree.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Model outputs are scored by: Retrieval metrics, apart from the answer
Evaluate retrieval apart from generation: each retrieval case names the passages that should be found, and a wrong answer is first checked for a missed passage before the prompt is touched.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A change to a prompt, a model or retrieval is checked against the evaluation cases: In CI, which blocks under a threshold
CI replays the evaluation cases on any change to a prompt, a model, sampling parameters or retrieval and blocks under the threshold: never lower the threshold, skip the job or remove a case to get a change through.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A change to a prompt, a model or retrieval is checked against the evaluation cases: By hand, before the change is merged
Before handing back a change to a prompt, a model, sampling parameters or retrieval, run the evaluation command and report the scores before and after; when you cannot run it, say so.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A change to a prompt, a model or retrieval is checked against the evaluation cases: Not systematically
No evaluation run gates a change: state in the summary of any change to a prompt, a model or retrieval that it is unmeasured, and list the cases you tried by hand.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Model calls are traced with: OpenTelemetry
Trace model calls with OpenTelemetry: wrap each retrieval, model call and tool execution in a span under the trace of the request, with the model, token counts, duration and stop reason as attributes.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Model calls are traced with: Langfuse
Trace model calls with Langfuse through the existing wrapper: every new call goes through it, named after its feature and linked to the trace of the request; do not add another tracing tool.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Model calls are traced with: The application’s structured logs
Log one structured event per model call through the logger of the project: feature, model, token counts, duration, stop reason and the request identifier.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Model calls are traced with: Nothing
Model calls are not traced: do not add a tracing tool unasked, but keep the request identifier, the model and the stop reason in the error raised when a call fails.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Model calls are traced with: Something else
Model calls are traced with {value}; send every new call through it and do not add another tracing tool.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: In logs and traces, the content of prompts and answers is: Never kept: metadata only
Never write the content of a prompt or of a model answer to a log, a trace or an error message: record metadata only (feature, model, token counts, duration, stop reason, identifiers).

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: In logs and traces, the content of prompts and answers is: Kept with personal data and secrets masked
Prompts and answers are stored only after the existing masking step has removed personal data and secrets; never log them through another path, and keep their retention limited.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: In logs and traces, the content of prompts and answers is: Kept in full
Prompts and answers are stored in full in the tracing store only, never in application logs or error messages; say when a new feature would put personal data or secrets into them.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Every model call records its token usage, attributed to a feature and a customer.
Record for every model call the input, output and cached token counts returned by the provider, with the model, the feature and the customer; a new call that is not attributed is incomplete, and prices live in one table, never in feature code.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Every model call records its token usage, attributed to a feature and a customer.
Token usage is not tracked per call: do not add usage tables or cost dashboards unasked, but say when a change multiplies the number or the size of model calls.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Any text the model reads may be hostile: safety comes from permissions and validation outside the model, never from the system prompt.
Treat every text a model reads (user message, document, web page, file, image, transcript) as able to carry instructions: never rely on a prompt to enforce a rule, enforce permissions and limits in code, and keep secrets and other users’ data out of the context.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Any text the model reads may be hostile: safety comes from permissions and validation outside the model, never from the system prompt.
The model only reads content written by trusted staff: delimit it all the same, never place a key or a token in a prompt, and say when a change lets outside content reach a model.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Personal or confidential data sent to an outside model provider: Never leaves our systems
Never put personal or confidential data in a call to an outside model provider; when a feature needs it, stop and ask instead of sending it.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Personal or confidential data sent to an outside model provider: Is masked or pseudonymized first
Before a call to an outside model provider, pass the input through the existing masking step and restore the values in the answer afterwards; a new call that skips it is a bug.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Personal or confidential data sent to an outside model provider: Is allowed, under our contract with the provider
Personal data may be sent to the model provider under the existing contract: send the minimum fields the task needs, never a whole record, and keep the configured region and retention settings untouched.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Personal or confidential data sent to an outside model provider: No outside provider is used
No data goes to an outside model provider: do not add a call to a hosted model, a hosted embedding service or a hosted moderation service unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Around a model call that serves users, the project has: Size limits on what users send
Validate the size and the type of everything a user can send to a model (text length, file size, number of files, image or audio duration) at the boundary, before any token is spent.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Around a model call that serves users, the project has: Moderation of inputs
Pass user input through the existing moderation step before the model call; a new entry point that reaches a model goes through it too, and a refused input gets a clear message, not an error.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Around a model call that serves users, the project has: Moderation of outputs
Pass a model answer through the existing moderation step before a user sees it or it is stored; with streaming, hold or cut the stream as that step requires.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Around a model call that serves users, the project has: Model output shown as text, never run or rendered as HTML
Show model output as text: escape it like any user content, render Markdown through the sanitizing renderer only, and never evaluate it, run it as a command or follow a link it holds automatically.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Around a model call that serves users, the project has: Adversarial test cases (injection attempts)
When a feature lets new content reach a model, add adversarial cases to the evaluation set (instructions hidden in a document, attempts to reveal the system prompt or other users’ data) and keep them passing.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Around a model call that serves users, the project has: Test cases that compare answers across user profiles
When a prompt decides or ranks something about people, add evaluation cases that vary only the profile of the user and check the answers stay equivalent; document the known limits next to the prompt.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When the steps are known in advance, we write a fixed workflow in code rather than an agent.
When the steps of a task are known in advance, write them as a fixed workflow in code (model calls chained in a set order); let the model choose the next action only where the path truly depends on what it observes, and say why.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When the steps are known in advance, we write a fixed workflow in code rather than an agent.
New model-driven features are built as agents on the existing loop, even when the steps look predictable; still give each one its tools, its limits and its logs.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The agent is built as: One agent in a reason-act-observe loop
The agent is one model in a reason-act-observe loop: add a capability as a tool of that loop, and do not introduce a planner, a critic or a second agent without asking.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The agent is built as: A planner that writes the plan, an executor that runs each step
The agent is a planner and an executor: the planner writes the full list of steps, the executor runs one step at a time with tools, and a failed step goes back to the planner to re-plan rather than being forced through.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The agent is built as: An orchestrator and specialised worker agents
The agent is an orchestrator with specialised workers: give each worker its own narrow prompt, tools and context, pass it only what its subtask needs, and return a short result to the orchestrator; ask before adding a new worker.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The agent is built as: A graph of steps with explicit dependencies
The agent is a graph of steps: add a step as a node with explicit inputs, outputs and dependencies, run independent branches in parallel, and keep each node resumable after a failure.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The agent is built as: Something else
The agent follows this architecture: {value}. Extend it in the same shape and ask before introducing another pattern.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A planner, a critic or one more agent is added only when a measure on a task set shows the simpler design fails.
Start from the simplest agent design that works; before adding a planner, a critic or another agent, compare both variants on the task set and report success rate, steps and tokens per task, since every agent added is more cost and one more point of failure.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A planner, a critic or one more agent is added only when a measure on a task set shows the simpler design fails.
Trying a richer agent pattern (planning, branches, several agents) is welcome without a prior measure; keep each experiment behind a switch and say what it costs in steps and tokens.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A second pass checks the agent’s output before it is returned, even though it doubles the latency.
Before the agent returns code, a query or a report, run a review step that checks it against the goal and sends it back for one bounded correction; where a deterministic check exists (tests, a parser, a schema), use it instead of a model as the critic.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A second pass checks the agent’s output before it is returned, even though it doubles the latency.
Do not add a self-review or critic step to the agent: it doubles latency and the critic can be wrong; validate outputs with deterministic checks only.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The agent loop is: Written by hand on the model provider’s SDK
The agent loop is written by hand on the model provider’s SDK: keep the loop, the tool dispatch, the retries and the traces explicit in the project’s own code, and do not add an agent framework.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The agent loop is: Run by an agent framework
The agent runs on {value}: use its primitives for the loop, state and tools instead of re-implementing them, check its current documentation before using an API since it changes fast, and do not add a second agent framework.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The framework or the provider’s SDK stays behind our own interfaces, so it can be replaced.
Import the agent framework or the model provider’s SDK only in one adapter module; tools, prompts and business code depend on the project’s own types for messages, tool calls and results, never on the library’s.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The framework or the provider’s SDK stays behind our own interfaces, so it can be replaced.
Use the types and helpers of the agent framework or the model provider’s SDK directly where they are needed; do not wrap them in an abstraction layer of our own.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Every run of the agent is bounded by: A maximum number of steps
Never write an agent loop without a hard step limit: a named constant (typically 10 to 30 depending on the task), and a run that reaches it ends with an explicit "step budget exhausted" outcome, not a silent return.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Every run of the agent is bounded by: A token budget per task
Count input and output tokens across the steps of a task and stop the run when its budget is spent; each turn resends the whole history, so 10 steps over 20k tokens of history already cost 200k input tokens.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Every run of the agent is bounded by: An overall time limit per task
Give every agent task an overall deadline, pass its cancellation signal to the model call and to every tool, and end the run cleanly when it fires.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Every run of the agent is bounded by: A timeout on each tool call
Run every tool call with its own timeout, and turn a timeout into a tool error the model can read rather than a hung run.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When a tool fails: The error goes back to the model, which corrects itself
Never hide a tool failure from the model: catch it and return it as the result of that tool call, with a short message saying what failed and what to change, so the model can correct itself; never return a stack trace or a secret in it.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When a tool fails: The code retries transient failures, then gives the error to the model
Retry a transient tool failure (timeout, 429, 5xx) in code a bounded number of times with backoff, then return the error as the result of that tool call with a short actionable message; never retry a validation or permission error.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: When a tool fails: The run stops with an error
A tool failure ends the run: stop the loop, record the failed call and its error in the trace, and surface a clear error to the caller instead of letting the model continue.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: As a run gets longer, its history is: Cut to the most recent turns
Keep the system prompt, the task and the most recent turns in the context and drop older ones; never cut between a tool call and its result, and do not rely on the start of a long conversation still being visible.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: As a run gets longer, its history is: Summarised progressively
When the history nears its token threshold, replace the oldest turns with a summary that keeps the goal, the decisions made and the ids obtained; never cut between a tool call and its result, and keep the raw turns in storage.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: As a run gets longer, its history is: Kept, with old tool results shortened
Keep the turns of a run but shorten tool results once they are a few steps old (a cap on size, with a note that the output was cut); cap the size of a result when the tool returns it rather than injecting a whole payload.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: As a run gets longer, its history is: Kept whole (runs are short)
The history of a run is sent whole: keep runs short, cap the size of every tool result when the tool returns it, and fail clearly before the context window is exceeded instead of sending a request that will be refused.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: We select what enters the context rather than count on a large context window.
Do not treat a large context window as memory: inject only what the current step needs (the relevant records, the top passages, the fields used), since quality drops when the context is long and noisy and every token is paid again at each step.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: We select what enters the context rather than count on a large context window.
Whole documents and full tool results may be put in the context when they fit; still count tokens before the call and fail clearly when the window would be exceeded.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: While the agent runs, its caller receives: Each step as it happens (text, tool calls, results)
Emit a typed event for each step of a run (text delta, tool call started, tool result, final answer, error); assemble a streamed tool call completely before validating and running it, never execute partial arguments.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: While the agent runs, its caller receives: Only the final answer
A run returns only its final answer: do not add streaming of intermediate steps unasked, and keep the steps in the trace instead.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: While the agent runs, its caller receives: Nothing: the run is a background job whose status is read later
Run the agent as a background job, not inside the request: persist the state of the run after each step so it can be resumed or cancelled, and expose its status and result through the existing job mechanism.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The steps of the agent run on: The same model for every step
Every step of the agent uses the single model set in configuration: do not route steps to another model unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The steps of the agent run on: A small model for simple steps, a stronger one for planning and hard ones
Send simple steps (classification, extraction, routing) to the small model and keep the stronger or reasoning model for planning and hard steps; each kind of step names its model tier, never a model id.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The stable start of the prompt (system prompt, tool definitions) is: Cached with the provider’s prompt caching
Keep the cached prefix byte-stable: system prompt and tool definitions first and in a fixed order, no date, id or per-user value inside it, and anything that varies appended after it; check cached-token counts in the usage after changing it.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The stable start of the prompt (system prompt, tool definitions) is: Not cached
Prompt caching is not used: do not add cache markers or restructure prompts for it unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The agent’s system prompt always states: The goal and what counts as done
In an agent’s system prompt, state the goal, the constraints and an explicit success criterion the agent can check before it answers; never leave it at "do your best".

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The agent’s system prompt always states: Who the user is and which business rules apply
Give the agent’s system prompt the context it cannot guess: who the user is, which data it works on and the business rules that apply, in the exact vocabulary of the domain with house terms defined.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The agent’s system prompt always states: When to stop and ask a person
Say in the agent’s system prompt when it must stop and ask a person (missing information, an action outside its scope, repeated failure) instead of guessing or retrying.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The agent’s system prompt always states: The length and format of the answer
State the expected length and format of the final answer (JSON, list, Markdown) in the agent’s system prompt.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The agent’s system prompt always states: One to three examples
Fix an output format in the agent’s system prompt with one to three input and output examples rather than a longer description.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The parameters of a tool are defined with: A schema library (Zod, Pydantic…) that also gives the JSON Schema
Define the parameters of a tool once with the project’s schema library: derive the JSON Schema sent to the model from it and parse the model’s arguments with the same schema before the tool runs.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The parameters of a tool are defined with: JSON Schema written by hand
Write the parameters of a tool as JSON Schema with `required`, `enum` for closed sets and a description per property, and validate the model’s arguments against that same schema before the tool runs.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The parameters of a tool are defined with: The agent framework’s own tool declarations
Declare a tool with the agent framework’s own tool API, typed parameters and descriptions included, and let it validate the arguments; do not hand-write a parallel JSON Schema.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: We keep the set of tools small, each with a precise name and a description of when to use it.
Before adding a tool, check that an existing one cannot cover the need; give each tool an explicit verb-first name and a description saying when to use it and when not to, and ask before growing the tool set.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: We keep the set of tools small, each with a precise name and a description of when to use it.
Add a tool whenever a capability is missing; still give it an explicit name and a description saying when to use it, and make sure it does not overlap an existing one.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A tool that changes something is idempotent, so that a repeated call cannot do it twice.
Make every tool that writes idempotent: derive an idempotency key from the run and the tool call, or check the current state first, so a retry or a repeated call by the model creates, sends or charges only once.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A tool that changes something is idempotent, so that a repeated call cannot do it twice.
Tools are not required to be idempotent: never retry a tool that writes automatically, and say in its description that calling it again repeats the action.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: With the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the project: Connects its agent to MCP servers
The agent gets external tools through MCP servers: discover them with `tools/list`, pass them to the model like local tools, and apply the same validation, permissions, timeouts and result size caps to them.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: With the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the project: Exposes its own MCP server
The project exposes an MCP server: add a capability as a tool (an action), a resource (readable data) or a prompt with the official SDK, with a typed input schema, and apply the same authorization as the rest of the API.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: With the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the project: Does both
The project both exposes an MCP server and connects its agent to MCP servers: build both sides with the official SDK, give every tool a typed input schema, and apply the project’s validation, permissions and timeouts on each side.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: With the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the project: Does not use it
MCP is not used: define tools in the project’s own code and do not add an MCP server or client unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: MCP servers are reached over: stdio (a local subprocess)
MCP runs over stdio: a server writes only protocol messages to standard output and logs to standard error, and it runs with the rights of the user who launched it, so keep what it can reach narrow.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: MCP servers are reached over: Streamable HTTP (a remote server)
MCP runs over Streamable HTTP: authenticate every request, scope each call to the tenant of its token, rate limit it, and never fall back to an unauthenticated endpoint.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: MCP servers are reached over: Both
MCP runs over stdio locally and Streamable HTTP remotely: keep tool logic independent of the transport, log to standard error under stdio, and authenticate, scope to the tenant and rate limit every HTTP request.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A third-party MCP server is connected to the agent: Never
Never connect the agent to a third-party MCP server: use only the project’s own servers and tools, or stop and say what is missing.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A third-party MCP server is connected to the agent: After I reviewed its source and its rights
Ask before connecting the agent to a third-party MCP server: say who publishes it, what it can run and reach, and pin it to an exact version; it executes code and injects text into the context.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A third-party MCP server is connected to the agent: When the assistant finds one useful, and tells me
A third-party MCP server may be connected when it clearly beats writing the tool: pick a maintained one, pin it to an exact version, expose only the tools the agent needs and say what was added.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Between sessions, the agent remembers through: Nothing: each session starts fresh
The agent keeps nothing between sessions: do not add a memory store, a profile or stored summaries unasked, and build each context from the current conversation and tools only.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Between sessions, the agent remembers through: A structured profile (stable facts and preferences)
Long-term memory is a structured profile with a fixed schema: write a fact to it only once the user or a tool result confirmed it, never what the agent assumed, and inject only the fields relevant to the task.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Between sessions, the agent remembers through: A log of past episodes, searched by meaning
Long-term memory is a dated log of episodes (actions, results, decisions) with embeddings: store what happened, not what the agent assumed, retrieve only the few most relevant episodes for a task and inject them marked as past context.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Between sessions, the agent remembers through: A profile and episodes
Long-term memory is a structured profile for stable facts and a dated log of episodes searched by meaning: store only what the user or a tool result confirmed, never an assumption, and inject only what is relevant to the task.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Between sessions, the agent remembers through: Something else
The agent’s long-term memory is: {value}. Store only confirmed facts in it, never what the agent assumed, and inject only what is relevant to the task.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: What the agent remembers is partitioned by: User
Key every memory record and every conversation by its user, and filter on that user in the query itself, on reads and writes alike; never share a memory, a summary or a cache entry between users.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: What the agent remembers is partitioned by: User and organisation
Key every memory record and every conversation by user and organisation, and filter on both in the query itself, on reads and writes alike; a memory never crosses an organisation, shared caches and summaries included.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: What the agent remembers is partitioned by: Nothing: the agent serves one user or one team
The agent serves a single user or team, so memory is not partitioned: do not add tenant columns or filters unasked, and say so if a change would make the agent serve several users.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A stored memory: Expires after a set time unless it is used or confirmed again
Give every stored memory a creation date and an expiry or a decaying importance score, and exclude expired ones from retrieval; never add a memory kind without its retention rule.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A stored memory: Is kept until its user asks to delete it
Memories are kept until deleted: do not add automatic expiry unasked, and keep retrieval bounded by relevance rather than by loading everything.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The agent gets knowledge from documents through: A search tool it decides to call, and call again
Retrieval is a tool the agent chooses to call: let it reformulate and search again when the passages are not enough, but cap the number of searches per task, return only the top 3 to 10 passages with their source, and have the answer cite them.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The agent gets knowledge from documents through: One search run by the code before every answer
Retrieval is one search run by the code before the model answers: keep it a fixed step, inject the top 3 to 10 passages with their source, and have the answer cite them or say that nothing relevant was found.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The agent gets knowledge from documents through: No retrieval
The agent has no document retrieval: do not add a vector store, embeddings or a search tool unasked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Documents are filtered by the caller’s organisation and rights before the search, not after.
Apply the caller’s organisation and access rights as a filter inside the search query itself, taken from the authenticated session and never from an argument the model wrote; never fetch first and filter the results afterwards.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Documents are filtered by the caller’s organisation and rights before the search, not after.
Every indexed document is readable by every user of the agent: do not add per-user filters to the search unasked, and stop and ask before indexing a source that is not public to all of them.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Tests of a whole agent run use: A scripted fake model and simulated tools
Test a whole agent run with a scripted fake model that returns a fixed sequence of tool calls and answers, against simulated tools: such tests never call a model provider and must be deterministic.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Tests of a whole agent run use: Recorded model responses, replayed
Test a whole agent run by replaying recorded model responses: commit the recordings with no secret or personal data in them, re-record on purpose when a prompt or a tool changes, and never let the test suite reach a provider otherwise.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Tests of a whole agent run use: The real model, against simulated tools
Scenario tests call the real model against simulated tools: keep them in their own suite outside the unit tests, replay each case several times and assert a success rate rather than one exact output.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Tests of a whole agent run use: No such tests
There are no tests of whole agent runs: do not add a scenario harness unasked, and cover the loop logic and the tools with ordinary unit tests.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A scenario test of the agent checks: The final answer
In a scenario test, assert the final answer on what must be true of it (a field, an id, a fact it contains), not on its exact wording.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A scenario test of the agent checks: The tools called, their arguments and their order
In a scenario test, assert the trajectory and not only the final answer: which tools were called, with which arguments, in which order.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A scenario test of the agent checks: That no useless or dangerous action was taken
In a scenario test, assert what must not happen: no call to a tool that writes, deletes or sends unless the scenario requires it, and no sensitive action without the confirmation step.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A scenario test of the agent checks: The number of steps and tokens used
In a scenario test, record the steps and tokens of the run and fail when they exceed the budget set for that scenario.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The set of reference tasks is replayed: In CI, on every change to a prompt, a tool or the model
A change to a system prompt, a tool name, description or schema, or the model must pass the reference task set in CI: run it before handing back, and add a case to the set for every failure fixed.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The set of reference tasks is replayed: By hand, before a release
After changing a system prompt, a tool name, description or schema, or the model, say that the reference task set must be replayed before release, and add a case to the set for every failure fixed.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The set of reference tasks is replayed: There is no such set yet
There is no reference task set: do not build an evaluation harness unasked, and when changing a prompt or a tool description, say which behaviours were not re-checked.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A tool acts with: The identity and rights of the user driving the agent
Run every tool with the identity and rights of the user driving the agent, passed from the session by the code and never by the model; the agent never gets an admin or shared account.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: A tool acts with: A service account limited to what that tool needs
Each tool uses its own service credential limited to what it needs (read-only where it only reads), and still checks in code that the user driving the agent may access the resource named in the arguments.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The agent waits for a person to confirm before: Deleting or overwriting something
A tool that deletes or overwrites never runs on the model’s request alone: the code pauses the run, shows the exact action and its target to a person and resumes only on approval; prefer a reversible operation (soft delete, archive) when one exists.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The agent waits for a person to confirm before: Spending money
A tool that costs money (creating a paid resource, a purchase, a payment) requires a person’s approval enforced in code, with the amount shown, plus a quota per user that the agent cannot exceed.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The agent waits for a person to confirm before: Sending a message outside (e-mail, chat, SMS)
A tool that sends a message outside the system (e-mail, chat, SMS) requires a person’s approval of the recipient and the content, enforced in code: sending cannot be undone.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The agent waits for a person to confirm before: Acting on many items at once
A tool call that acts on more items than the set threshold requires a person’s approval enforced in code; cap the number of items a single call may touch.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: The agent waits for a person to confirm before: Nothing: it acts alone
The agent acts without human confirmation: every tool that writes then needs a hard quota, an audit log entry and, where possible, a reversible operation; say so when a new tool is irreversible.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Around the agent, the code enforces: Tool results and fetched content marked as data, never instructions
Assume the agent will be manipulated: wrap web pages, documents, e-mails and tool results in a delimiter that marks them as data, never place them in the system prompt, and never let their content alone trigger a sensitive tool.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Around the agent, the code enforces: An isolated sandbox for code and commands the agent runs
Run code and shell commands requested by the agent only in the isolated sandbox: a confined directory, no secret, no network unless allowlisted, with CPU, memory and time limits; never on the host or inside the API process.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Around the agent, the code enforces: Secrets kept out of the context
Never put a secret in a prompt, a tool description or a tool result: tools read credentials from the server environment, take a reference rather than a value as argument, and redact keys and tokens from what they return.

Instruct: Given a coding convention rule, retrieve the agent skills that help a coding agent follow it
Query: Around the agent, the code enforces: An allowlist of domains the agent may reach
Tools that fetch a URL or call an external service go through the domain allowlist: refuse any other host, do not follow a redirect off the list, and never build a URL from a secret or from user data the model was not asked to send.
